posts.body:
I’ve redone my website again. I think I’m keeping this one!!!!
I keep changing it because I never really know what someone takes away from it. I know what I’m trying to say about myself, but does that actually come across when someone spends a minute looking? (Part of doing what I do is having your work and what you build constantly perceived and critiqued)
This time I went stupid simple. My projects, what they actually do, and my resume. Some portfolios get a little carried away (yes, I’m talking about you, WebGL warriors). I don't want to play a video game to learn about you (I don't end up learning about you). Typeset font. All in a lowkey, lo-fi, lo-tech way.
Obviously, I still left some Easter eggs.
In this day and age I have spent a lot of time getting good at using AI to code, regardless, finding random hidden things in video games was one of my favorite parts of playing them as a kid. So just to make sure I still got it I implemented a feature all by myself (I know so crazy), if you spam click my profile picture too quickly, it grows rocket boosters and flies off the page. Probably unnecessary, but that part makes me happy.
I think this version feels more like me. Hopefully I can leave it alone long enough for someone else to actually see it.
Take a look: https://abhikhur.com
And if you’re hiring, especially take a look. I’m studying computer science and mathematics at UT Dallas and looking for more software engineering and research opportunities. <333

posts.body: I’ve been working on GridironDEX, an interactive football reference and play-design tool I built because most football glossaries stop at definitions.  It now has 105 reviewed concepts covering formations, coverage, fronts, blocking, special teams, and more. The tactical mode lets you choose personnel, draw routes, test calls against randomized defensive looks, and play through full drives.  The interesting engineering problem was keeping the diagram, simulation, contact timing, ball movement, and outcome logic on one deterministic clock. I built it with React and TypeScript.  Try it here: https://gridiron-dex.com  #React #TypeScript #SportsAnalytics #SportsTechnology
